mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which can stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher during periods of declining FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 4% signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns remain positive when UNRATE exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth coupled with stable inflation indicates a healthy economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If positive returns do not follow strong GDP growth and stable inflation (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production indicates increased supply, which can lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO rises (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS increases (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% indicates tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns remain positive when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates weak demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in real federal spending signals increased demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS increases (t-test p > 0.05).
